requirements.subject: ent:stop-statement
requirements.canonical: The `stop` statement SHALL terminate the execution of a test component, a test case or the control behaviour.
requirements.original: The stop statement terminates execution of test components, a test case or a test control.

ambiguity.issue: "test control" is used instead of the glossary term "control behaviour" (module control function).

requirements.subject: ent:stop-statement
requirements.canonical: The `stop` statement has the syntax `stop`.
requirements.original: stop

requirements.subject: ent:stop-statement
requirements.canonical: The `stop` statement terminates execution in different ways depending on the context in which it is executed.
requirements.original: The stop statement terminates execution in different ways depending on the context in which it is executed.

requirements.subject: ent:stop-statement
requirements.condition: the stop statement is executed in a control behaviour
requirements.canonical: When executed in a control behaviour, the `stop` statement SHALL terminate the execution of the control component.
requirements.original: When executed in a control behaviour, it terminates the execution of the control component.

requirements.subject: ent:stop-statement
requirements.condition: the stop statement is invoked in a test case, altstep or function executed on a test component
requirements.canonical: When invoked in a test case, altstep or function executed on a test component, the `stop` statement SHALL terminate that test component.
requirements.original: When invoked in a test case, altstep or function that are executed on a test component, it terminates the relevant test component.

requirements.subject: ent:stop-statement
requirements.canonical: A `stop` statement that terminates a test component IS semantically identical to the stop component operation `self.stop`.
requirements.original: NOTE: The semantics of a stop statement that terminates a test component is identical to the stop component operation self.stop (see clause 21.3.3).

requirements.subject: ent:return-statement
requirements.canonical: The `return` statement SHALL terminate the execution of a function or altstep.
requirements.original: The return statement terminates execution of functions or altsteps.

requirements.subject: ent:return-statement
requirements.canonical: The `return` statement has the syntax `return` optionally followed by an Expression or a TemplateInstance.
requirements.original: return [ Expression | TemplateInstance ]

requirements.subject: ent:return-statement
requirements.canonical: The `return` statement SHALL return control to the point from which the function or altstep was called.
requirements.original: The return statement terminates execution of a function or altstep and returns control to the point from which the function or altstep was called.

requirements.subject: ent:return-statement
requirements.condition: the return statement is used in a function
requirements.canonical: A `return` statement used in a function MAY be associated with a return value or template.
requirements.original: When used in functions, a return statement may be optionally associated with a return value or template.

readings: A `return` statement in a function MAY be associated with a return value or template, and SHALL be so exactly when the function has a return clause.
A `return` statement in a function MAY be associated with a return value or template regardless of the function's return clause.
ambiguity.issue: "optionally" is read as depending on the return clause of the function (chosen, consistent with clause 16.1); it could also be read as an unconditional option.

requirements.subject: ent:alt-statement
requirements.canonical: An altstep call within an `alt` statement MAY be followed by an optional statement block.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 allows optional statement blocks that may follow altstep calls within alt statements.

requirements.subject: ent:return-statement
requirements.condition: a statement block follows the altstep call within the alt statement
requirements.canonical: If a statement block follows the altstep call in an `alt` statement, the `return` statement in the altstep SHALL return control to the beginning of that statement block.
requirements.original: If there is a statement block, the return statement returns control to the beginning of this statement block and the statement block is executed before the alt statement is left.

requirements.subject: ent:statement-block
requirements.condition: a statement block follows the altstep call within the alt statement
requirements.canonical: If a statement block follows the altstep call in an `alt` statement and the altstep is left by a `return` statement, the statement block SHALL be executed before the `alt` statement is left.
requirements.original: If there is a statement block, the return statement returns control to the beginning of this statement block and the statement block is executed before the alt statement is left.

requirements.subject: ent:return-statement
requirements.condition: no statement block follows the altstep call within the alt statement
requirements.canonical: If no statement block follows the altstep call in an `alt` statement, test execution SHALL continue with the first statement following the `alt` statement after the `return` statement in the altstep is executed.
requirements.original: If there is no statement block, test execution continues with the first statement following the alt statement.

requirements.subject: ent:return-statement
requirements.canonical: The return value or template of a `return` statement SHALL be evaluated before control is returned.
requirements.original: The return value or template is first evaluated before returning.

requirements.subject: ent:return-statement
requirements.canonical: A `return` statement SHALL NOT be present in a testcase definition.
requirements.original: a) The return statement shall not be present in testcase definitions.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: The `log` statement provides the means to write logging information to some logging device.
requirements.original: The log statement provides the means to write logging information to some logging device.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain a module parameter identifier as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: module parameter identifier; What is logged: actual value

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a module parameter identifier is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When a module parameter identifier is used in a `log` statement, the actual value of the module parameter IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: module parameter identifier; What is logged: actual value

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain a literal value as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: literal value; What is logged: value; Comment: This includes also free text.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a literal value is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When a literal value is used in a `log` statement, the value IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: literal value; What is logged: value; Comment: This includes also free text.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A literal value used as a log item in a `log` statement IS allowed to be free text.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: literal value; What is logged: value; Comment: This includes also free text.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain a data constant identifier as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: data constant identifier; What is logged: actual value

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a data constant identifier is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When a data constant identifier is used in a `log` statement, the actual value of the constant IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: data constant identifier; What is logged: actual value

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain a template instance as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: template instance; What is logged: actual template or field values and matching symbols

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a template instance is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When a template instance is used in a `log` statement, the actual template or field values and matching symbols IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: template instance; What is logged: actual template or field values and matching symbols

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain a variable identifier as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: variable identifier; What is logged: actual value or "UNINITIALIZED"; Comment: See notes 3 and 4.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a variable identifier is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When a variable identifier is used in a `log` statement, the actual value of the variable or "UNINITIALIZED" IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: variable identifier; What is logged: actual value or "UNINITIALIZED"; Comment: See notes 3 and 4.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain a `self`, `mtc`, `system` or component type variable identifier as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: self, mtc, system or component type variable identifier; What is logged: actual value and if assigned the component instance name otherwise "UNINITIALIZED"; Comment: On logging actual values see notes 2 to 4. Actual component states shall be logged according to note 5.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a `self`, `mtc`, `system` or component type variable identifier is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When a `self`, `mtc`, `system` or component type variable identifier is used in a `log` statement, the actual value and, if assigned, the component instance name, otherwise "UNINITIALIZED" IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: self, mtc, system or component type variable identifier; What is logged: actual value and if assigned the component instance name otherwise "UNINITIALIZED"; Comment: On logging actual values see notes 2 to 4. Actual component states shall be logged according to note 5.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a self, mtc, system or component type variable identifier is logged
requirements.canonical: When a `self`, `mtc`, `system` or component type variable identifier is logged, the actual component state SHALL be logged as one of Inactive, Running, Stopped or Killed.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: self, mtc, system or component type variable identifier; What is logged: actual value and if assigned the component instance name otherwise "UNINITIALIZED"; Comment: On logging actual values see notes 2 to 4. Actual component states shall be logged according to note 5.

readings: The actual component state SHALL be logged in addition to the actual value and component instance name.
The actual component state SHALL be logged only when the component state is logged at all; the column only requires the value and instance name.
ambiguity.issue: The "What is logged" column does not mention the component state while the comment requires it; chosen reading: the state is logged in addition to the value and name.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain a `create` operation as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: create operation; What is logged: actual state and the component instance name; Comment: The actual state is always set to Inactive.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a `create` operation is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When a `create` operation is used in a `log` statement, the actual state and the component instance name IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: create operation; What is logged: actual state and the component instance name; Comment: The actual state is always set to Inactive.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a create operation is logged
requirements.canonical: When a `create` operation is logged, the logged actual state IS always Inactive.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: create operation; What is logged: actual state and the component instance name; Comment: The actual state is always set to Inactive.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain a `running` operation (component or timer) as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: running operation (component or timer); What is logged: return value; Comment: true or false. In case of component or timer arrays, array element specification shall be included.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a `running` operation (component or timer) is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When a `running` operation (component or timer) is used in a `log` statement, the return value (true or false) IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: running operation (component or timer); What is logged: return value; Comment: true or false. In case of component or timer arrays, array element specification shall be included.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: the `running` operation applies to an array
requirements.canonical: When a `running` operation on a component or timer array is logged, the array element specification SHALL be included.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: running operation (component or timer); What is logged: return value; Comment: true or false. In case of component or timer arrays, array element specification shall be included.

readings: A `running` operation used as log item on a component or timer array SHALL include the array element specification in the log statement argument.
The logged output of a `running` operation on an array SHALL include the array element specification.
ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether the array element specification has to be written in the log statement argument (a restriction) or included in the logged output; chosen reading: the argument shall contain the element specification.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain an `alive` operation (component) as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: alive operation (component); What is logged: return value; Comment: true or false. In case of arrays, array element specifications shall be included.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: an `alive` operation (component) is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When an `alive` operation (component) is used in a `log` statement, the return value (true or false) IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: alive operation (component); What is logged: return value; Comment: true or false. In case of arrays, array element specifications shall be included.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: the `alive` operation applies to an array
requirements.canonical: When a `alive` operation on a component or timer array is logged, the array element specification SHALL be included.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: alive operation (component); What is logged: return value; Comment: true or false. In case of arrays, array element specifications shall be included.

readings: A `alive` operation used as log item on a component or timer array SHALL include the array element specification in the log statement argument.
The logged output of a `alive` operation on an array SHALL include the array element specification.
ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether the array element specification has to be written in the log statement argument (a restriction) or included in the logged output; chosen reading: the argument shall contain the element specification.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain a `checkstate` operation as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: checkstate operation; What is logged: return value; Comment: true or false.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a `checkstate` operation is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When a `checkstate` operation is used in a `log` statement, the return value (true or false) IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: checkstate operation; What is logged: return value; Comment: true or false.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain a port instance as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: port instance; What is logged: actual state; Comment: Port states shall be logged according to note 6.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a port instance is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When a port instance is used in a `log` statement, the actual state of the port IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: port instance; What is logged: actual state; Comment: Port states shall be logged according to note 6.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a port instance is logged
requirements.canonical: When a port instance is logged, the port state SHALL be logged as Started or Stopped.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: port instance; What is logged: actual state; Comment: Port states shall be logged according to note 6.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain a default type variable identifier as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: default type variable identifier; What is logged: actual state or "UNINITIALIZED"; Comment: Default states shall be logged according to note 7. See also notes 2 to 4.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a default type variable identifier is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When a default type variable identifier is used in a `log` statement, the actual state of the default or "UNINITIALIZED" IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: default type variable identifier; What is logged: actual state or "UNINITIALIZED"; Comment: Default states shall be logged according to note 7. See also notes 2 to 4.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a default type variable identifier is logged
requirements.canonical: When a default type variable identifier is logged, the default state SHALL be logged as Activated or Deactivated.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: default type variable identifier; What is logged: actual state or "UNINITIALIZED"; Comment: Default states shall be logged according to note 7. See also notes 2 to 4.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain an `activate` operation as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: activate operation; What is logged: activate operation; Comment: The actual state is always set to activated.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: an `activate` operation is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When an `activate` operation is used in a `log` statement, the activate operation (its actual state) IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: activate operation; What is logged: activate operation; Comment: The actual state is always set to activated.

readings: When an `activate` operation is logged, the actual state of the resulting default (Activated) IS logged.
When an `activate` operation is logged, a textual representation of the activate operation itself IS logged.
ambiguity.issue: The "What is logged" column says "activate operation", which does not name a loggable item; chosen reading: the actual state of the activated default (comment: "always set to activated").

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: an activate operation is logged
requirements.canonical: When an `activate` operation is logged, the logged actual state IS always Activated.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: activate operation; What is logged: activate operation; Comment: The actual state is always set to activated.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain a timer name as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: timer name; What is logged: actual state; Comment: Timer states shall be logged according to note 8.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a timer name is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When a timer name is used in a `log` statement, the actual state of the timer IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: timer name; What is logged: actual state; Comment: Timer states shall be logged according to note 8.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a timer is logged
requirements.canonical: When a timer is logged, the timer state SHALL be logged as Inactive, Running or Expired.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: timer name; What is logged: actual state; Comment: Timer states shall be logged according to note 8.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain a `read` operation as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: read operation; What is logged: return value; Comment: See clause 23.4.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a `read` operation is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When a `read` operation is used in a `log` statement, the return value IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: read operation; What is logged: return value; Comment: See clause 23.4.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain a `match` operation as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: match operation; What is logged: return value; Comment: true or false.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a `match` operation is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When a `match` operation is used in a `log` statement, the return value (true or false) IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: match operation; What is logged: return value; Comment: true or false.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain a `valueof` operation as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: valueof operation; What is logged: return value

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a `valueof` operation is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When a `valueof` operation is used in a `log` statement, the return value IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: valueof operation; What is logged: return value

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain a `getverdict` operation as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: getverdict operation; What is logged: return value; Comment: none, pass, inconc, or fail.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a `getverdict` operation is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When a `getverdict` operation is used in a `log` statement, the return value (none, pass, inconc or fail) IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: getverdict operation; What is logged: return value; Comment: none, pass, inconc, or fail.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain a predefined function invocation as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: predefined functions; What is logged: return value; Comment: See annex C.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a predefined function invocation is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When a predefined function invocation is used in a `log` statement, the return value IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: predefined functions; What is logged: return value; Comment: See annex C.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain a function instance as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: function instance; What is logged: return value; Comment: Only functions with return clause are allowed.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a function instance is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When a function instance is used in a `log` statement, the return value IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: function instance; What is logged: return value; Comment: Only functions with return clause are allowed.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: a function instance is used as log item
requirements.canonical: A function instance used as a log item in a `log` statement SHALL refer to a function with a return clause.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: function instance; What is logged: return value; Comment: Only functions with return clause are allowed.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.canonical: A `log` statement MAY contain an external function instance as a log item.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: external function instance; What is logged: return value; Comment: Only external functions with return clause are allowed.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: an external function instance is used in a log statement
requirements.canonical: When an external function instance is used in a `log` statement, the return value IS logged.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: external function instance; What is logged: return value; Comment: Only external functions with return clause are allowed.

requirements.subject: ent:log-statement
requirements.condition: an external function instance is used as log item
requirements.canonical: An external function instance used as a log item in a `log` statement SHALL refer to an external function with a return clause.
requirements.original: Used in a log statement: external function instance; What is logged: return value; Comment: Only external functions with return clause are allowed.
